s1.syndrome_frame: Progressive visual impairment with night blindness and scotomas
salient_findings: Night blindness since childhood
Inferonasal scotoma on Goldmann visual field
Abnormal electroretinogram with flat rod response
Hypofluorescence on fundus autofluorescence
Inner retinal thickening and disorganization on OCT
key_facts: Patient age 42
Symptoms present since childhood
No symptoms except night blindness
Visual acuity 20/25 to 20/30 in both eyes
Color vision normal
Fundus examination shows few yellow spots
Indistinct grayish circle beyond the arcades
Electroretinogram shows large, slow scotopic and photopic responses
Fundus autofluorescence shows hypofluorescence in superotemporal zones
OCT shows central macula with clear layers
Perifoveal region with supernormal thickness
Parafoveal region with 95% thickness
Foveal region with normal thickness
Eccentric areas with marked inner retinal thickening and disorganization

shortlist.label: Retinitis pigmentosa
shortlist.why_kept: Night blindness since childhood, abnormal electroretinogram, and fundus examination findings

shortlist.label: Choroideremia
shortlist.why_kept: Progressive visual impairment, night blindness, and scotomas, with characteristic fundus autofluorescence and OCT findings

shortlist.label: Gyrate atrophy
shortlist.why_kept: Night blindness, scotomas, and characteristic fundus examination findings, including yellow spots and an indistinct grayish circle

shortlist.label: Leber congenital amaurosis
shortlist.why_kept: Night blindness since childhood, with severe visual impairment and characteristic electroretinogram and OCT findings

shortlist.label: Cone-rod dystrophy
shortlist.why_kept: Progressive visual impairment, night blindness, and scotomas, with abnormal electroretinogram and fundus examination findings

raw.rationale: The patient's night blindness since childhood, normal color vision, and specific findings on electroretinogram, fundus autofluorescence, and OCT are consistent with retinitis pigmentosa, which typically presents with night blindness and progressive visual field loss.

rejected.label: Choroideremia
rejected.why: Choroideremia typically affects the choroid, retina, and retinal pigment epithelium, with more pronounced choroidal atrophy, which is not the primary finding in this case.

rejected.label: Gyrate atrophy
rejected.why: Gyrate atrophy is characterized by well-defined areas of chorioretinal atrophy, which are not described in this patient's fundus examination.

rejected.label: Leber congenital amaurosis
rejected.why: Leber congenital amaurosis typically presents with severe visual impairment or blindness at birth, which does not match this patient's relatively preserved visual acuity.

rejected.label: Cone-rod dystrophy
rejected.why: Cone-rod dystrophy typically presents with decreased visual acuity and color vision defects, which are not prominent in this case, and the specific pattern of retinal changes does not align with the described findings.
